name: Directional Stimulus Prompting (DSP)
executive_summary: Train a small policy model to generate short hints (like keywords the output should include) inserted into the prompt to steer a frozen, black-box LLM — optimize the hint-generator, not the LLM or base prompt.
description: Rather than optimizing the prompt text directly (APE) or evolving a prompt population (Promptbreeder), DSP optimizes a small auxiliary policy model whose only job is to produce query-specific hints — for example, keywords a summary should include — which are then inserted into an otherwise-fixed prompt template before it goes to the large black-box LLM. The policy model is trained with reinforcement learning using the downstream LLM's output quality as the reward signal, making this a way to steer a frozen LLM's behavior without ever fine-tuning the LLM itself or hand-searching over full prompt text.
when_to_use: Steering a frozen, black-box LLM (API-only access, no fine-tuning) toward query-specific desired properties, where a small auxiliary model can be trained to generate the steering hints.
when_not_to_use: A fixed, task-agnostic prompt already performs adequately — training and maintaining a separate policy model is only worth it when per-query steering matters.
known_pitfalls: Requires a working RL training loop for the policy model, including a usable reward signal derived from the downstream LLM's output quality — more infrastructure than a static prompt-optimization method.

primary_source.authors: Li, Peng, He, Galley, Gao, Yan
primary_source.title: Guiding Large Language Models via Directional Stimulus Prompting

variables.name: stimulus_type
variables.description: What kind of hint the policy model produces, e.g. keywords for a summary

variables.name: generated_stimulus
variables.description: The policy model's generated hint for this specific query

variables.name: base_prompt_template
variables.description: The otherwise-fixed prompt template the stimulus is inserted into

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: This template describes a training-time process (fine-tuning or policy training), not a single reproducible inference call; reproducibility depends on the training pipeline and data, not on prompt text alone.
